searchText: This should be easy for the CL, has there been a PR in the engine API repo? We could trivially send blobs on reorgs, we already have to reimport a bunch of operations This sentence there seems to imply that this was discussed and rejected by CL devs, I'd like to be pointed to where this discussion happened Hi Tim, is the recording available? One of the arguments against that is `newPayload` call delayed until all blobs are received from the network This is different though. It's only on reorg. You call `newPayload` with reorg'ed blobs. Not current blobs I see, so it requires an optional `blobs` field in the method and a logic of traversing reorged blocks which can be implementation specific. Curious what EL client devs thinking on exposing a separate optional method for this purpose. Optional meaning that it can be a no op if a client doesn't support this feature Newpayload is out of the question, but Peter's comment is about reintroducing, which is not a hot path for us, we can send blobs in the background on reorgs Yeah, I can see now. I am thinking that we can introduce a method to pass blobs and implement the logic after the HF and roll it out in uncoordinated fashion to avoid delaying Dencun by this additional chunk of work I'd persoanlly be favoring not worrying about delay but spend enough time and get this right before the fork I still think this would be an unnecessary abstraction breaking that brings dubious value recovering blob TXs to the mempool from sophisticated users that bypassed the mempool I would say that if one as submitted a block transaction that for any reason is not in the justified/finalized chain then it should be re-submitted anyway. The reasons for that can be different and reorgs would be just one of them I checked how Arbitrum works today. Sequencer does resubmit reorg'ed call data tx and it won't forget about it until it has been finalized
